sets.name: Research
sets.covers: Interviews, surveys, usability test plans, synthesis, personas and journey maps.
sets.why: Left alone, Claude will write you a persona from nothing. This set gives it a method for asking real people first.

entries.name: design-research
entries.author: MC Dean
entries.summary: Personas, empathy maps, journey maps, interview scripts, surveys, diary studies, card sort analysis, usability test plans and synthesis.

entries.name: lenny-skills research set
entries.author: RefoundAI
entries.summary: customer-interviews and analyzing-user-feedback, from a much larger skills library.
entries.installNote: Copy the skill folders you want into your project's .claude/skills/ directory.

entries.name: customer-research
entries.author: Corey Haines
entries.summary: Customer research from a marketing point of view.

sets.name: Design systems
sets.covers: Tokens, components, naming, governance and documentation.
sets.why: Claude reaches for whatever value looks right. These hold it to the tokens and components you already chose.
sets.missing: Mine enforce a system you already have. Nothing of mine builds one.

entries.name: design-systems
entries.author: MC Dean
entries.summary: Tokens, component specs, naming, theming, icons, motion systems, governance, pattern libraries and accessibility audits.

entries.name: Design System Enforcer
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Checks UI code against a design system's tokens and components.
entries.proof: Ships with its own test suite.
entries.installNote: Clone the repo and add it as an MCP server. The README has the steps.

entries.name: design-system agent
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Drives live page violations to zero without changing how a page looks unless a person approves it.

sets.name: Information architecture
sets.covers: Content inventories, card sorts, taxonomies, labels, sitemaps, navigation, URL rules, content models, redirects, tree tests and findability.
sets.why: Where things go decides whether anyone finds them. It's also the one set with a skill tested end to end.
sets.missing: The eleven focused skills split from the original aren't published yet. In one run of the same three test cases, the split scored 28 of 29 and the single skill 25 of 29.

entries.name: information-architecture
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude, rewritten from lyndonkl/claude, RavenClaude and jarango.com
entries.summary: Content inventories, card sorts, taxonomies, sitemaps, navigation, URL rules, content models, tree tests, redirect plans and findability metrics.
entries.proof: 3 test cases, 3 rounds, every grade public. Latest round: 28 of 29 with the skill, 19 of 29 without. Chosen on 9 of 10 requests and none of 10 near-misses.

entries.name: content-inventory
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Lists what a site or corpus holds and audits it: keep, revise, merge or retire. Samples large sets and says so.
entries.proof: Checking script with its own self-test.

entries.name: card-sort
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Plans open, closed and hybrid card sorts and analyses the results: similarity, clusters and cards with no clear home.
entries.proof: Analysis script with its own self-test.

entries.name: taxonomies
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Categories, tags, facets and controlled vocabularies, tested by applying them to the real content, with a governance loop.
entries.proof: Checking script with its own self-test.

entries.name: sitemaps
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Decides the structure of a site, app or docs set: shape, depth, template types and one home for every item.
entries.proof: Checking script with its own self-test.

entries.name: navigation
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Menus, sidebars, footers, breadcrumbs and tab bars, with an entry rule for each surface and a plan for mobile and keyboard.

entries.name: labeling
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Names for sections, menus and categories in the users' own words, checked with a predictability test.
entries.proof: Checking script with its own self-test.

entries.name: content-models
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Content types, fields and relations for each template, and how the model constrains authors.

entries.name: url-structure
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: URL rules and slug conventions a platform can enforce, and an audit of the URLs that exist.
entries.proof: Checking script with its own self-test.

entries.name: redirect-maps
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Old-to-new URL maps for migrations and rebuilds, checked for chains, loops and coverage of every old URL.
entries.proof: Checking script with its own self-test.

entries.name: tree-tests
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Plans tree tests and analyses the results: success with confidence intervals, directness and first clicks.
entries.proof: Analysis script with its own self-test.

entries.name: findability
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Works out why people can't find things, analyses search logs, and sets up synonyms, best bets and measures.
entries.proof: Search-log script with its own self-test.

sets.name: Interaction design
sets.covers: States, forms, feedback, errors, navigation patterns, UX laws and motion.
sets.why: The happy path is the easy part. This set covers what happens on an error, during a load and when someone changes their mind.

entries.name: interaction-design
entries.author: MC Dean
entries.summary: States, forms, feedback, errors, loading, search, navigation patterns, micro-interactions and UX laws such as Fitts and Hick.

entries.name: Emil Kowalski motion skills
entries.author: Emil Kowalski
entries.summary: animation-vocabulary, improve-animations, review-animations, emil-design-eng and apple-design.

sets.name: Visual design
sets.covers: Hierarchy, colour, type, layout, visual critique and page craft.
sets.why: Hierarchy and type are where AI-made pages start to look alike. These give Claude a way to see that and correct it.

entries.name: ui-design
entries.author: MC Dean
entries.summary: Colour, type scale, spacing, layout grid, responsive design, dark mode, visual hierarchy, platform conventions and the Gestalt laws.

entries.name: visual-critique
entries.author: MC Dean
entries.summary: Critiques hierarchy, colour, typography, composition, affordance, information density and brand consistency.

entries.name: impeccable
entries.author: Paul Bakaus
entries.summary: Designs, critiques, audits, polishes and animates frontends.

entries.name: landing-page-design
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Copy strategy and look before any code, a hero-first build, gates against generic AI pages and a two-reviewer feedback round.
entries.proof: One dry run and two critic passes. The UX-OS landing page went through it too.

entries.name: Taste skills
entries.author: Leonxlnx
entries.summary: Frontend taste skills. This repo holds design-taste-frontend, and the high-end, minimalist and brutalist styles now live in taste-skill-classics.

sets.name: Prototyping
sets.covers: Wireframes, user flows, concept selection, prototype strategy, test plans and heuristic evaluation.
sets.why: A prototype exists to kill an idea cheaply. This set decides what to build, how rough it can be and what counts as a pass.

entries.name: prototyping-testing
entries.author: MC Dean
entries.summary: Wireframe specs, user flows, parallel concepts, concept selection, prototype strategy, test scenarios, click tests, heuristic evaluation, accessibility test plans and A/B tests.

entries.name: prototype
entries.author: Matt Pocock
entries.summary: Builds a quick prototype to test an idea.

sets.name: UX strategy
sets.covers: Problem framing, briefs, vision, opportunities and metrics.
sets.why: A fast answer to the wrong problem is still wrong. This set makes Claude frame the problem before it touches a screen.

entries.name: ux-strategy
entries.author: MC Dean
entries.summary: Problem framing, briefs, north star vision, opportunity frameworks, metrics, service blueprints, content strategy and its own information-architecture skill.

entries.name: design-strategy
entries.author: MC Dean
entries.summary: Design vision, strategy documents, org-level principles, investment cases and portfolio prioritisation.

sets.name: AI-XD
sets.covers: AI experience design: conversation, trust, guardrails and agent handoffs.
sets.why: Designing for a model is its own discipline. Trust, refusal, handoff and recovery all need designing on purpose.
sets.missing: Three more packs are installed and switched off.

entries.name: model-interaction-design
entries.author: MC Dean
entries.summary: Conversation patterns, mixed-initiative flow, generative UI, context windows and frustration detection.

entries.name: ai-alignment-reasoning
entries.author: MC Dean
entries.summary: Guardrails, harm anticipation, trust calibration, transparency, consent and escalation.

entries.name: design-agent-orchestration
entries.author: MC Dean
entries.summary: How agents collaborate, hand off, recover from failure and stay legible to people.

entries.name: evaluation
entries.author: MC Dean
entries.summary: Behaviour evals, trust calibration and failure analysis for agentic experiences.

entries.name: prompt-architecture
entries.author: MC Dean
entries.summary: Structures prompts and context as a design material.

entries.name: system-behavior-shaping
entries.author: MC Dean
entries.summary: Defaults, guardrails, refusals and behavioural contracts.

sets.name: Accessibility and inclusion
sets.covers: Inclusive personas, cognitive access, accessible content and adaptive interfaces.
sets.why: Access decided at the end gets cut. This set starts with who's being left out.
sets.missing: Five of the six packs are switched off.

entries.name: inclusive-personas
entries.author: MC Dean
entries.summary: Personas, user stories and scenarios that include disability from the start.

entries.name: accessibility-decisions
entries.author: MC Dean
entries.summary: Documents and maintains accessibility decisions across teams and time.

entries.name: accessible-content
entries.author: MC Dean
entries.summary: Content that works for screen readers, cognitive differences and diverse literacy.

entries.name: adaptive-interfaces
entries.author: MC Dean
entries.summary: Design systems that respect user preferences and adapt to individual needs.

entries.name: cognitive-accessibility
entries.author: MC Dean
entries.summary: Cognitive load, plain language, wayfinding and focus.

entries.name: inclusive-interaction
entries.author: MC Dean
entries.summary: Multi-modal interactions that adapt to how people move, perceive and communicate.

sets.name: Design ops and communication
sets.covers: Handoff, critique process, sprints, rationale and case studies.
sets.why: Good design still has to survive the handoff and the meeting. This set covers what happens around the file.
sets.missing: Eleven program and leadership packs are switched off.

entries.name: design-ops
entries.author: MC Dean
entries.summary: Handoff specs, critique and review process, design QA, sprints, design debt and impact reporting.

entries.name: designer-toolkit
entries.author: MC Dean
entries.summary: Design rationale, case studies, presentations, UX writing, negotiation and design-system adoption.

entries.name: UX program and leadership packs
entries.author: MC Dean
entries.summary: Eleven packs: program-planning, stakeholder-comms, delivery-execution, cross-functional-alignment, measurement-ops, process-design, people-management, team-building, org-influence, operating-cadence and leadership-craft.
entries.installNote: All eleven are in the same marketplace. Install the ones you want by name from the /plugin menu.

sets.name: Orchestration
sets.covers: Running the other sets against a real target until it meets a bar.
sets.why: The other sets are methods. This one runs them against a real page and keeps going until it holds up.

entries.name: crit and critique-partner
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Interviews you about a page, then critiques it against your own written rules and loops until a verifier passes it.
entries.proof: A gate with 55 test cases, and two headless runs.
entries.installNote: Needs Node 18 or later and Playwright with Chromium.

entries.name: Design Agent
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: A self-looping designer: critique, fix, re-render and re-score until an exit bar is met, then learn from the run.
entries.proof: An independent critic scores every pass.

entries.name: feature-plan
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Interviews you into a spec, a design brief and build slices, then runs the feature pipeline.

entries.name: feature-build
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Builds one slice of a planned feature and loops it until lint, tests, the design system and review all pass.
entries.proof: An independent reviewer scores every pass.
